exclusions.name: Any other customs broker or employee at Marchwood
exclusions.why_safe: Malik is the only licensed broker at Marchwood, and no one else may prepare or submit an entry (e1, e12). Excluding others is safe because they cannot perform the required steps.

exclusions.name: Any other person at Sanko Kikai besides Tamesada
exclusions.why_safe: Tamesada is the only person authorized to issue or correct a certificate of origin (e6). Excluding others is safe because they cannot provide the missing document.

exclusions.name: Any other document or requirement
exclusions.why_safe: The only missing item is the corrected certificate of origin (e4, e14). All other documents are complete and in Malik's possession. Excluding other potential issues is safe because they are not needed.

exclusions.name: Public holidays or system outages
exclusions.why_safe: No public holidays occur on the relevant dates (e3), and the port authority system operates normally (e13). Excluding these is safe because they would not affect the timeline.

uncertainties.meaning: Whether Tamesada received Malik's email before boarding her flight. The email was sent at 3:40 PM Eastern on Monday 16 November, which is 5:40 AM Japan time on 17 November. Her flight departed Osaka at 10:10 PM Japan time on 16 November, which is 8:10 AM Eastern on 16 November. So the email was sent after her departure. She had no means of receiving email while in flight. She landed at 4:30 AM Singapore time on 17 November, which is 3:30 PM Eastern on 16 November. So she could receive the email after landing. But it is uncertain whether she checked her email before clearing the arrivals hall, or whether she cleared her inbox within 45-60 minutes as per her pattern. The evidence says she clears her compliance inbox between 45 and 60 minutes after landing, before leaving the airport. So she likely receives the email around 4:15-4:30 AM Singapore time (3:45-4:00 PM Eastern) on 17 November. However, the exact time is uncertain.

Whether Tamesada issues the corrected certificate on 17 November after receiving the request. She is the only authorized person, and issuing takes 20 minutes. She has a pattern of dealing with pending certificates before anything else. But it is uncertain if she will do so on this occasion, given that she is traveling and may have other priorities. The evidence does not guarantee she will issue it immediately.

Whether Malik receives the corrected certificate before the deadline. Even if Tamesada issues it on 17 November, Malik is out of the office on Tuesday 17 November and does not check email. He returns to work on Wednesday 18 November at 8:00 AM Eastern. The deadline is 9:00 AM Eastern. So he would have only one hour to prepare and submit the entry. But it is uncertain if the certificate arrives before 8:00 AM on Wednesday, or if it arrives during his email checks at 8:00, 8:30, 9:00 etc. The email delivery is within 2 minutes, so if Tamesada sends it anytime before 8:00 AM Eastern on Wednesday, Malik will see it at 8:00 AM. But if she sends it after 8:00 AM, he might see it at 8:30 or later, leaving insufficient time to prepare and submit before 9:00 AM.

Whether Malik can prepare and submit the entry within the available time. He needs 45 minutes of working time. If he receives the certificate at 8:00 AM, he can start immediately and finish by 8:45 AM, then submit. The system operates 24/7. So that would be in time. But if he receives it at 8:30 AM, he would finish at 9:15 AM, after the deadline. So the timing is critical and uncertain.
